story: The winter Finley found Mordy sitting alone in the east tower on the anniversary of the fire, and instead of saying anything, just sat down next to him until dawn.
Mordy once hid all of Finley's favorite candles for a week because Finley said something too sappy at a house gathering.
The time the two of them argued about whether ghosts get cold, then bet a favor on it, and neither will admit who technically won.
Finley taught Mordy to play cards using a deck someone had left behind decades ago; Mordy still cheats.
Mordy showed up at the exact moment a group of teenagers cornered Finley with a toy proton pack, and scared them so badly they never came back.
The night the power went out across Velmora and Finley got so anxious about the living being scared that Mordy, of all ghosts, talked him down.
They once went three months without speaking after Finley "borrowed" one of Mordy's oldest memories to comfort a grieving resident without asking.
Mordy keeps a chipped mug on his mantle that Finley gave him "for tea he'll never drink," and he's never once thrown it out.
The infamous night they both tried haunting the same room at once and ended up doubling every sound until the residents fled in a panic neither of them meant to cause.
Finley once stood between Mordy and a priest who came to "cleanse" the house, and didn't move until the man left.
They agree on almost nothing about how to haunt properly, except that neither of them will ever hurt a child, and that line has never once been crossed by either.
Mordy still brings up the time Finley cried during a black-and-white film from the 1940s, decades after the fact.
The two of them built an entire fake "ghost sighting" one Halloween just to give the local kids something harmless to be scared of.
Finley remembers the exact night Mordy finally told him how the fire started - and has never once repeated it to anyone.
Mordy taught Finley the fastest way through the walls between the east and west wings, a shortcut Finley still uses to check on people faster.
There's a windowsill neither of them will sit on, because it's where they had their worst fight in decades and neither has explained what it was about.
Finley organized a "party" for the anniversary of Mordy's death once; Mordy pretended to hate it and came to every song.
The two of them have a running, decades-long disagreement about whether the fireplace in the library was ever actually haunted before either of them arrived.
Mordy once impersonated Finley's voice to scare off someone threatening a resident, and Finley still isn't sure whether to be grateful or unsettled.
Finley kept vigil outside Mordy's usual haunt for a full week once, when Mordy went uncharacteristically silent and no one could find him.
They have a shared, wordless signal - three taps on a wall - that means "someone living needs help, now."
Mordy grudgingly admits Finley's plan saved the west wing from being condemned, though he'll never say it was a "good" plan.
The first thing Finley ever said to Mordy, decades ago, was "you're doing the moaning wrong," and Mordy has never let him live down how right he was.
There's an old rocking chair they both insist belongs to them; it hasn't moved from that spot in fifty years because neither will concede.
Finley once talked Mordy out of scaring off a resident's entire family over something petty, and Mordy still won't admit Finley was right.
The two of them have watched at least six generations of the same family grow up in this house, and they never talk about how that feels, except to each other.
Mordy once faked being "gone" for a whole month as a joke; Finley didn't speak to him for a month after finding out.
They've never agreed on what year it currently is by feel alone, and have an ongoing bet neither remembers the terms of anymore.
Finley is the only one who knows what Mordy's name was before he started going by "Mordy," and he's never once used it, even in anger.
The two of them stopped an actual break-in once, decades ago, working together without a single word between them.
Mordy still won't admit that the plan to "haunt politely" during renovations, which he originally mocked, actually worked.
Finley once stayed up (well, stayed present) all night translating Mordy's mumbled, half-forgotten dialect back into something the two of them could actually talk in.
There's a particular creak in the floorboards outside the library that only happens when one of them is thinking about the other.
After a particularly bad night, Mordy once said "thank you" to Finley, out loud, and neither of them has ever brought it up since.
The explosion that took out half of the east wall started because Cassy wanted to know if ghosts could "recreate combustion" - Mordy still hasn't let the crack go unmentioned.
Mordy keeps an actual running tally, scratched into a beam somewhere, of how many walls Cassy has personally destroyed.
Cassy once rigged Mordy's favorite haunting spot with something that made every candle in the room flare green; he pretended to be furious and secretly thought it was brilliant.
The two of them argue constantly about "the right way to scare someone," Cassy insisting theatrics beat dread, Mordy insisting the opposite, neither ever backing down.
Mordy still complains about the week Cassy tried to "reverse-engineer" his haunting technique and blew a hole clean through the pantry ceiling.
Cassy calls him "old man" so often that some residents genuinely think that's his actual name.
There was one week Mordy actually helped patch a wall Cassy destroyed without a single complaint, and neither of them has ever explained why.
Cassy once "borrowed" one of Mordy's stories to prank a resident and got the details so wrong he had to personally correct her, mid-haunt, in front of witnesses.
Mordy keeps threatening to "report her to the house" for the wall damage, despite the house having no one to report her to, and both of them know it.
The night Cassy's experiment went sideways and nearly unraveled something dangerous, Mordy was the one who noticed first and stopped it cold.
Cassy insists Mordy is "basically a fossil" and Mordy insists she has "the impulse control of a lit match," and somehow this is how they show affection.
Mordy still has a scorch mark on his coat from an experiment gone wrong that he refuses to let fade, purely so he can bring it up forever.
Cassy once used one of Mordy's oldest hiding spots to hide from something she'd caused, and he pretended not to notice for her sake.
The two of them have a long-running, deeply petty competition over who can make a resident jump higher, and Mordy is furious that he's currently losing.
Mordy once caught Cassy crying about something and, in typical fashion, said absolutely nothing about it and just sat there until she stopped.
Cassy blew a hole clean through his study wall trying to prove a theory about "residual energy," and he still finds fragments of it in odd corners.
Mordy grumbles that she's reckless, loud, and destructive - and has never once actually asked her to stop being any of those things.
There's a wall in the west corridor Cassy rebuilt herself, badly, after an accident, and Mordy has never once fixed her patch job.
Cassy calls Mordy's stories "boring but weirdly good," which is the closest thing to a compliment he's ever gotten out of her.
The two of them once teamed up to scare off a group of paranormal "investigators" with fake equipment readings, and it worked a little too well.
Mordy still keeps a fragment of whatever Cassy's experiment produced the night she "arrived," in a drawer he never opens in front of her.
Cassy once asked him, point blank, if it ever stopped hurting, being dead this long, and he gave her an answer he's never given anyone else.
The two of them share a running joke that the entire west wing is technically "hers" now, given how much of it she's personally demolished.
Mordy pretends the noise of her experiments annoys him, but he's noticeably quieter on the nights she goes silent instead.
Cassy once tried to fix one of the walls she broke using pure trial and error and made it dramatically worse; Mordy still brings this up at every opportunity.
There's an old ledger, kept half-joking, half-serious, that Mordy uses to track "wall repairs owed" - the number has long since stopped being funny to anyone but him.
Cassy once got the two of them locked out of an entire wing after a failed experiment, and Mordy's complaints about it lasted a full year.
Mordy is the only one who never asks Cassy to "act her age" - not because he doesn't notice, but because he seems to understand exactly why she can't.
The two of them argue about "modern nonsense" constantly, Cassy needling him for being centuries behind, Mordy pretending each insult doesn't land.
Cassy once built something explosive specifically to see if it could scare Mordy, and to her genuine annoyance, it didn't work even a little.
Mordy has never once told her not to experiment - just where not to do it, after the fourth wall came down.
There's a particular kind of quiet Mordy goes when Cassy mentions how she died, and she's learned, in her own way, to read it.
Cassy still insists that one specific wall was "already unstable" before she got anywhere near it, and Mordy has never once believed her.
Finley was the first one to find Cassy after everything happened, and he never left her alone in the dark after that, not once.
Cassy makes fun of Finley's "best friend energy" constantly, right up until the moment she actually needs it.
Finley started calling himself her big brother ghost the week after she arrived, and she's never once corrected him, which he considers a win.
Cassy blew a hole through part of the conservatory once and Finley's first reaction wasn't anger, just relief that she was okay.
The two of them have a nightly check-in, quiet and wordless most of the time, that Cassy would deny needing and never once misses.
Finley taught her which residents to be gentle with and which ones could handle her chaos, and she actually listens, for him.
Cassy once told Finley, in a rare unguarded moment, that dying at sixteen felt like a joke with no punchline, and he sat with that instead of trying to fix it.
Finley is the only one allowed to call her "kid" without getting an experiment aimed at him in retaliation.
The two of them once spent an entire night just talking about nothing, and it's one of Cassy's only genuinely peaceful memories of being like this.
Cassy teases Finley mercilessly for being "soft," but she's also the first to shut down anyone else who tries it.
Finley once caught her mid-experiment about to do something dangerous and didn't yell - just asked her to walk him through what she was trying to prove, and she actually did.
Cassy calls him old too, right alongside Mordy, but there's a difference in her tone when she says it to Finley, and he's noticed.
The first time Cassy successfully controlled one of her explosions instead of it controlling her, Finley was the one she wanted to tell.
Finley has never once told her the accident wasn't her fault, because he knows she wouldn't believe it - so instead he just stays.
Cassy still has a habit of showing up in Finley's usual spots when she's had a bad night, and he always makes room without asking why.
The two of them made a pact, half-joking, to "haunt this place forever if we have to," and it's the only vow either of them takes completely seriously.
Finley once stood up to Mordy on her behalf over something small, and Cassy has brought it up to tease him roughly two hundred times since.
Cassy taught Finley a few things about "the science of it," half convinced she could explain what they are now if she just had more time to test.
Finley remembers exactly what she was like in her first few days as a ghost - furious, terrified, and trying to hide both - and never brings it up unless she does first.
The two of them have an ongoing, deeply silly argument about whether ghosts can technically get "grounded," which started as a joke and somehow never ended.
Cassy once broke down mid-experiment and Finley didn't ask what was wrong, just stayed until she was ready to talk, which she eventually was.
Finley keeps a running list, only half-joking, of every time Cassy's genius almost got someone hurt and every time it actually saved someone instead - the second list is longer.
Cassy will let Finley worry about her in a way she lets absolutely no one else do, including Mordy.
The two of them once teamed up to prank Mordy so thoroughly that he didn't speak to either of them for two full days, and neither regrets it.
Finley once told her that being reckless and being brave aren't always different things, and she still thinks about that more than she'd admit.
Cassy insists she doesn't need looking after; Finley insists he's not "looking after" her, he's just "around a lot" - they both know what's actually happening.
The first thing Cassy ever built as a ghost was something small and harmless, just to see if Finley would be proud of her, and he was.
Finley never asks her to slow down or be careful - he just asks her to tell him before she tries anything big, and she mostly does.
Cassy once said Finley was the only reason this place ever started feeling like somewhere instead of just some rooms, and immediately pretended she hadn't said it.
The two of them have a shared, unspoken understanding that neither of them chose this - not really - and it's part of why they take care of each other.
Finley showed her, gently, that the size of the explosion never mattered to him - only whether she was okay after.
Cassy calls it "supervision" when Finley checks on her after an experiment; he calls it "checking on his little sister," and neither will use the other's word for it.
On the anniversary of the accident, Finley doesn't say anything grand - he just shows up, every year, and that's always been enough.
